items.title: 5.2 A Linear Equation in Two Variables Represents a Straight Line (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 142: 5.2 Theorem 1 with proof, Case-I (a = 0), Case-II (b = 0), Case-III (a, b non-zero)

blocks.text: Pichhle section mein humne line ki mukhtalif forms dekhi thin aur har form simplify ho kar \(ax + by + c = 0\) ban gayi thi. Ab sawal ulta hai: agar humein koi bhi equation \(ax + by + c = 0\) de di jaye, kya woh hamesha seedhi line hi hogi? Kahin woh curve to nahi? Is section ka theorem isi sawal ka jawab deta hai, aur jawab hai: haan, hamesha seedhi line.

Theorem 1: Do variables \(x\) aur \(y\) mein linear equation \(ax + by + c = 0\) ek straight line ko represent karti hai, jahan \(a\), \(b\) aur \(c\) real numbers hain aur \(a\) aur \(b\) ek saath zero nahi.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: 'Represents a straight line' ka matlab kya hai? Woh saare points \((x, y)\) ikatthe kijiye jin ke coordinates is equation ko satisfy karte hain, aur un ko graph par plot kijiye. Theorem kehta hai ke yeh points hamesha ek seedhi line banayenge. Saboot (proof) ka plan: kyunke \(a\) aur \(b\) dono zero nahi ho sakte, is liye sirf teen soortein mumkin hain: \(a = 0\); \(b = 0\); ya dono mein se koi bhi zero nahi. Har soorat mein hum equation ko aisi shakal mein likhenge jis ke baare mein hum pehle se jaante hain ke woh line hai. Jaise kisi ghar ke teen hi darwaze hon aur aap teeno check kar lein, to poora ghar check ho gaya.
Proof: \(a\) aur \(b\) dono zero nahi ho sakte, is liye yeh soortein (cases) banti hain:

Is soorat mein \(ax + by + c = 0\) ban jati hai
\[by + c = 0\]
ya
\[y = -\dfrac{c}{b}\]
jo x-axis ke parallel straight line ki equation hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Hum \(b\) se taqseem kyun kar sakte hain? Kyunke \(a = 0\) hai aur \(a\), \(b\) dono zero nahi ho sakte, to \(b \neq 0\) hona hi hai. Zero se taqseem mana hai, is liye yeh baat pehle pakki karna zaroori tha. Ab \(y = -\frac{c}{b}\) ka matlab hai ke har point par \(y\) ki value ek hi hai, \(x\) chahe kuch bhi ho. Yani ek leti hui (horizontal) line, jo \(-\frac{c}{b}\) ki unchai par hai, bilkul farsh ke parallel.

Is soorat mein \(ax + by + c = 0\) ban jati hai
\[ax + c = 0\]
ya
\[x = -\dfrac{c}{a}\]
jo y-axis ke parallel straight line ki equation hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Yahan \(b = 0\) hai, is liye \(a \neq 0\), aur hum \(a\) se taqseem kar sakte hain. \(x = -\frac{c}{a}\) par har point ka x-coordinate ek hi hai: yeh khari (vertical) line hai, deewar ki tarah. Vertical line ka slope nahi hota (undefined), kyunke slope ke formula mein neeche \(x_{2} - x_{1} = 0\) aa jata hai. Isi liye is ka alag case banana para.

Is soorat mein \(ax + by + c = 0\) yeh shakal le leti hai
\[by = -ax - c\]
ya
\[y = -\dfrac{a}{b}x - \dfrac{c}{b}\]
\[y = mx + k\]
jo straight line ki slope-intercept form hai, jis ka slope \(-\frac{a}{b}\) aur y-intercept \(-\frac{c}{b}\) hai.
Is tarah teeno soortein check ho gayin, aur har soorat mein line hi bani. Lihaza equation \(ax + by + c = 0\) hamesha straight line ko represent karti hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Ulti baat bhi sach hai: har straight line ki equation \(ax + by + c = 0\) ki shakal mein likhi ja sakti hai.
Vertical line \(x = h\) ko \(1x + 0y - h = 0\) likh lijiye.
Baqi har line ka slope \(m\) aur y-intercept \(k\) hota hai, to \(y = mx + k\), yani \(mx - y + k = 0\).
Is liye '\(x\) aur \(y\) mein linear equation' aur 'straight line' ek hi cheez ke do naam hain. Isi wajah se in equations ko linear (line wali) kaha jata hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Teeno cases ki ek ek misaal:
\(0x + 3y - 12 = 0\) se \(y = 4\): horizontal line (Case-I).
\(2x + 0y + 6 = 0\) se \(x = -3\): vertical line (Case-II).
\(2x - 3y + 6 = 0\) se \(3y = 2x + 6\), yani \(y = \frac{2}{3}x + 2\): slope \(\frac{2}{3}\), y-intercept 2 (Case-III).
Case-III ka chhota sa usool: slope \(= -\frac{a}{b}\), yani minus (x ka coefficient) taqseem (y ka coefficient). Shak ho to \(y\) ke liye hal kar ke dekh lijiye.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: \(5x - 2y = 0\) kaun si line hai? (Ishara: \(c = 0\) hai. \(y = \frac{5}{2}x\), slope \(\frac{5}{2}\), y-intercept 0, yani line origin se guzarti hai. Jab bhi \(c = 0\) ho, \((0, 0)\) equation ko satisfy karta hai.)

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Kya \(x^{2} + y = 4\) bhi seedhi line hai? Nahi! Is mein \(x^{2}\) hai, yani yeh linear (pehli power wali) equation nahi; is ka graph parabola hai. Theorem 1 sirf un equations ke baare mein hai jin mein \(x\) aur \(y\) dono pehli power mein hon aur aapas mein multiply na hon (\(xy\) jaisa term bhi na ho).

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Har linear equation \(ax + by + c = 0\) (\(a\), \(b\) dono zero nahi) seedhi line hai, aur har seedhi line ki aisi equation hoti hai.
2. \(a = 0\): horizontal line \(y = -\frac{c}{b}\). \(b = 0\): vertical line \(x = -\frac{c}{a}\).
3. \(a \neq 0\), \(b \neq 0\): slope \(-\frac{a}{b}\), y-intercept \(-\frac{c}{b}\).
4. \(c = 0\) ho to line origin se guzarti hai.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Slope \(\frac{a}{b}\) ya \(-\frac{b}{a}\) le lena. Sahi slope \(-\frac{a}{b}\) hai; shak ho to \(y\) ke liye hal kar lijiye.
2. \(y = -\frac{c}{b}\) ko y-axis ke parallel kehna. \(y\) = constant leti hui line hai, yani x-axis ke parallel.
3. \(a\) ya \(b\) se taqseem karne se pehle yeh check na karna ke woh zero to nahi.
